topic: The first human heart transplant: Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town, South Africa, 3 December 1967 (Christiaan Barnard; patient Louis Washkansky lived 18 days)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: The first heart transplant was performed in the United States.
myths.reality: US teams (Shumway, Lower) developed the technique, but the first human-to-human transplant was Barnard's in Cape Town on 3 December 1967; the first US adult transplant followed in January 1968 (Shumway, Stanford).

wiki_washkansky.title: Louis Washkansky
wiki_washkansky.notes: recipient of the first human heart transplant 3 Dec 1967; died 21 Dec 1967 of pneumonia, 18 days after surgery

wiki_barnard.title: Christiaan Barnard
wiki_barnard.notes: performed the world's first human-to-human heart transplant 3 December 1967 at Groote Schuur, Cape Town; became an international celebrity

stanford_med.title: Norman Shumway and the history of heart transplantation
stanford_med.notes: Shumway's lab developed the technique over a decade; first US adult heart transplant 6 January 1968 at Stanford, a month after Barnard

wiki_shumway.title: Norman Shumway
wiki_shumway.notes: Stanford surgeon, pioneer of heart transplantation research; first US adult heart transplant January 1968

statpearls_denerv.title: Physiology, Cardiac Denervation / Heart transplant physiology
statpearls_denerv.notes: the transplanted heart is denervated — no autonomic nerve connection to the recipient's nervous system; rhythm is set by the donor sinoatrial node (intrinsic pacemaker)

cleveland_transplant.title: Heart Transplant
cleveland_transplant.notes: a transplanted heart has no nerve connections; it beats via its own SA node and responds to hormones rather than nerve signals

pmc_barnard50.title: The first human heart transplant and further advances in cardiac transplantation at Groote Schuur Hospital
pmc_barnard50.notes: Brink & Hassoulas 2017: Washkansky operated 3 Dec 1967; good cardiac function; died day 18 of pneumonia (Pseudomonas) under heavy immunosuppression

claims.text: The first human-to-human heart transplant was performed by Christiaan Barnard at Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town, South Africa, on 3 December 1967; the recipient was Louis Washkansky.
vo: the first human heart transplant happened in which country
united states, south africa, or united kingdom
south africa. cape town, december 1967: surgeon christiaan barnard gave louis washkansky a new heart

claims.text: Washkansky lived 18 days after the operation and died of pneumonia on 21 December 1967; the transplanted heart was functioning.
vo: the patient lived 18 days. the heart worked; it was pneumonia that killed him

claims.text: Norman Shumway's team at Stanford developed the surgical technique; Barnard performed the first human operation and became internationally famous; the first US adult transplant followed in January 1968.
vo: stanford had done the research, but barnard got there first, and was famous overnight

claims.text: A transplanted heart is denervated — it has no nerve connection to the recipient's brain — and beats because of its own intrinsic pacemaker, the sinoatrial node.
vo: a transplanted heart has no nerves linking it to the brain. it beats on its own pacemaker, inside the muscle
screen: its own pacemaker keeps the beat
